title: DOM: selecting, creating and changing elements

videos.script:
Ten lessons were the language. {{seam}} Today the browser starts, and for three lessons the subject is the page: what a script can see of it, how it reacts to a person, and how it waits.

When a browser reads a page, it does not keep the text of the HTML. {{tree}} It builds a tree of objects, one for every element and every piece of text, and that tree is what you see drawn on the screen. It is called the DOM, the Document Object Model.

{{change}} A script changes what is on the screen by changing the tree. Find an element, change its text, give it a class, add a new one. The browser notices and draws the result.

{{list}} Most of that is a short list of methods, and you will learn them today. Finding elements with the same selectors a stylesheet uses. Changing their text, their classes and their data. Building new ones from a template. And walking from one element to the ones around it, which is how a click on a button finds the row it belongs to.
